_comment: AIOS MCP server registration for the triangulation session.
AIOS exposes its 30+ commands (memory query, spec scan, steering, etc.)
as MCP tools so a Claude/Codex/etc. session can invoke them.
Drop this snippet into your IDE/CLI MCP config:
- Codex CLI: ~/.codex/mcp.json (or wherever Codex reads MCP from)
- VS Code Claude extension: workspace settings .vscode/settings.json
Replace the placeholder paths/keys before use.
_usage: Once registered, in the session you can ask AIOS to:
- Query past memory:    'aios: what did we learn about CWE-798?'
- Run a spec scan:      'aios: scan platform_synth/ for spec drift'
- List steering docs:   'aios: list steering for backend/'
- Diff against memory:  'aios: diff /api/auth/refresh against memory'
do NOT depend on AIOS MCP — they run via plain shell. AIOS adds the
qualitative model-driven layer ON TOP of those automated outputs.
If you don't have AIOS installed, skip this file; the triangulator
still works with two sources, it just labels findings as 2/2 instead of 3/3.
